mcqs.q: The autonomic nervous system controls all of the following EXCEPT:
mcqs.explain: The autonomic (visceral) system is involuntary; it controls BP, heart rate, GI activity and glandular secretions — not voluntary skeletal movement.

mcqs.q: The SYMPATHETIC nervous system is also called:
mcqs.explain: Sympathetic = adrenergic = sympathomimetic ('fight or flight'); parasympathetic = cholinergic ('rest and digest').

mcqs.q: The adrenergic neurotransmitters (catecholamines) are:
mcqs.explain: The catecholamine transmitters are epinephrine (prototype) and norepinephrine, secreted by the adrenal gland.

mcqs.q: The four main adrenergic receptors are:
mcqs.explain: Adrenergic receptors are α1, α2, β1 and β2 (with dopamine D1/D2 as a separate catecholamine receptor family).

mcqs.q: An α1-agonist such as phenylephrine causes:
opts: Vasoconstriction and a rise in blood pressure
mcqs.explain: α1 stimulation (phenylephrine) causes vasoconstriction and raises blood pressure.

mcqs.q: A β1-agonist such as dobutamine mainly acts on the:
opts: Heart — increasing rate and force (and BP)
mcqs.explain: β1 receptors are on the heart; dobutamine increases heart rate and force of contraction (and BP).

mcqs.q: A β2-agonist such as salbutamol produces:
mcqs.explain: β2 receptors are on bronchial smooth muscle; salbutamol relaxes them, relieving bronchospasm in asthma.

mcqs.q: The α2-agonist clonidine is used to:
opts: Lower blood pressure (and manage opioid withdrawal)
mcqs.explain: α2 stimulation provides feedback inhibition; clonidine lowers BP and is used in opioid-withdrawal management (so is methyldopa).

mcqs.q: Catecholamines are enzymatically degraded by:
mcqs.explain: Adrenergic transmitter action is ended by α2 feedback and enzymatic degradation by MAO and COMT.

mcqs.q: On the eye, adrenergic drugs cause:
mcqs.explain: Adrenergic drugs lower intraocular pressure and cause mydriasis (pupil dilation).

mcqs.q: A metabolic effect of β-receptor stimulation is:
mcqs.explain: β-stimulation increases glycogenolysis, raising blood glucose (hyperglycaemia) — relevant in diabetics.

mcqs.q: On the salivary glands, adrenergic drugs cause:
mcqs.explain: Adrenergic drugs vasoconstrict the salivary glands, reducing salivary flow (a cause of dry mouth).

mcqs.q: Why is epinephrine added to local anaesthetics in dentistry?
opts: Its vasoconstriction prolongs anaesthesia, reduces toxicity and gives a dry field
mcqs.explain: Epinephrine causes vasoconstriction that limits diffusion of the LA — prolonging its action, lowering systemic toxicity and providing a drier surgical field.

mcqs.q: Adverse reactions to adrenergic drugs are an extension of their effects and include:
opts: Anxiety, tremor, tachycardia, raised BP and arrhythmias
mcqs.explain: Adverse effects mirror the pharmacology: anxiety, tremor, tachycardia, increased blood pressure and arrhythmias.

mcqs.q: Antiadrenergic drugs lower blood pressure by:
opts: Reducing sympathetic tone and total peripheral resistance
mcqs.explain: Antiadrenergic drugs reduce sympathetic tone in blood vessels, decreasing peripheral resistance and blood pressure.

mcqs.q: Propranolol is an example of a:
mcqs.explain: Propranolol (and nadolol) are non-selective β-blockers; atenolol and metoprolol are selective β1-blockers.

mcqs.q: A SELECTIVE β1-blocker is:
mcqs.explain: Atenolol and metoprolol are selective β1-blockers; propranolol and nadolol block both β1 and β2.

mcqs.q: Adverse reactions of β-blockers include:
opts: Bradycardia, hypotension, fatigue and orthostatic hypotension
mcqs.explain: β-blockers cause bradycardia, hypotension (including orthostatic), drowsiness/fatigue and sometimes diarrhoea.

mcqs.q: Salbutamol is therapeutically used as a:
mcqs.explain: Salbutamol is a β2-agonist bronchodilator used in asthma; adrenaline is also a bronchodilator and cardiac stimulant.

mcqs.q: Ephedrine is commonly used as a:
mcqs.explain: Ephedrine is used as a nasal decongestant and CNS stimulant; terbutaline/orciprenaline are uterine relaxants/bronchodilators.

mcqs.q: An α1-BLOCKER such as prazosin will:
mcqs.explain: Blocking α1 vasoconstriction lowers blood pressure; prazosin is used for hypertension and BPH.

mcqs.q: Which drug is the prototype catecholamine?
mcqs.explain: Epinephrine (adrenaline) is the prototype catecholamine, with direct action at the nerve ending.

saqs.q: Give the synonymous terms for the sympathetic and parasympathetic systems.
saqs.a: Sympathetic = adrenergic = sympathomimetic ('fight or flight'). Parasympathetic = cholinergic = parasympathomimetic ('rest and digest').

saqs.q: Match each receptor to an agonist and its main effect: α1, α2, β1, β2.
saqs.a: α1 phenylephrine → ↑BP; α2 clonidine → ↓BP; β1 dobutamine → heart (↑rate/force); β2 salbutamol → bronchodilation.
By α2 feedback inhibition and enzymatic degradation by MAO and COMT.

saqs.q: List the pharmacologic effects of adrenergic drugs on the CV, respiratory and salivary systems.
saqs.a: CV: ↑ rate, force, BP, peripheral resistance. Respiratory: bronchodilation. Salivary: vasoconstriction → ↓ flow.

saqs.q: Explain why epinephrine is combined with local anaesthetics.
saqs.a: Epinephrine causes vasoconstriction, limiting LA diffusion → prolongs anaesthesia, reduces systemic toxicity, and creates a dry field.

saqs.q: Differentiate non-selective and selective β-blockers with examples.
saqs.a: Non-selective (β1+β2): propranolol, nadolol. Selective β1: atenolol, metoprolol. Both lower BP.
